hints.content:
Kathy earns $\blueD{\$15}$ for mowing lawns and $\greenD{\$35}$ for delivering newspapers each week.

$\blueD{15} + \greenD{35}$

She did this for $\maroonD{20}$ weeks, so we multiply the expression by $\maroonD{20}$. To show that we are multiplying the whole expression by $\maroonD{20}$, we can put the expression $\blueD{15} + \greenD{35}$ in parentheses.

$\maroonD{20}\times(\blueD{15} + \greenD{35})$

This tells us that everything inside the parentheses is being multiplied by $\maroonD{20}$.
At the end of the $20$ weeks, she spent $\$\purpleD{300}$ for her bike, so we will subtract $\purpleD{300}$ from $\maroonD{20}\times(\blueD{15} + \greenD{35})$.

question.content:
Kathy worked for $20$ weeks so she could buy a bike for $\$300$.

The table below shows the amount of money she earned each week. She made the same amount of money each week.

Job | Money earned
:- | :-
Mowing lawns | $\$15$
Delivering newspapers | $\$35$

**Which numerical expression shows the amount of money Kathy has left after buying her bike?**   

[[☃ radio 1]]
